subject: Kickoff: European data residency MAP & stakeholder alignment for EuroFin

Subject: Kickoff: European data residency MAP & stakeholder alignment for EuroFin

Hi Sophie / Marco,

Thanks again for the time earlier — per our call this morning I wanted to start a short mutual action plan (MAP) thread to align stakeholders, responsibilities, and a tight close timeline for the EU data residency evaluation. Goal is to get to a signed pilot agreement and a validated residency posture within six weeks.

Proposed quick agenda / roles:
- EuroFin: Sophie (security lead), Marco (platform) — provide residency requirements, approvals, and legal review.
- Redwood: Rafael (deal lead), Marissa (solutions / evaluation), Laura (compliance).
- Third-party: Cathal from RegConsult for cross-border guidance as needed.

Immediate asks:
1) Can you confirm the internal approvers and a single point of contact for legal/Procurement?
2) Any regulatory boundaries beyond standard EU data localization we should know about (e.g., country-specific mandates)?

I attached a first-pass MAP workbook and a residency checklist (draft) to help us capture milestones and owners. Marissa will propose concrete evaluation steps (test dataset, latency targets, audit access) by tomorrow.

If this looks good, I’ll schedule a 30-min MAP kickoff with all stakeholders for early next week.

Best,
Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Quick confirmations:
- Approvers: Anna Moreau (Head of InfoSec), Benoît Lambert (Legal counsel) — both should be looped when we have the MAP/timebox.
- POC for procurement: Marco (cc’d).
- Country constraints: We operate primarily in FR/DE/IE and we have a standing requirement that customer-identifiable logs must not leave the EU without approval.

Proposed attendees for kickoff: Anna Moreau (InfoSec), Benoît Lambert (Legal), Marco (Platform), Sophie (Security), Rafael, Marissa, Laura.

Subject: Re: Kickoff: European data residency MAP & stakeholder alignment for EuroFin

Folks — I attached a draft MAP workbook (EuroFin_MAP_v0.1.xlsx) with the following initial milestones:
- Week 0 (this week): Stakeholder list + kickoff meeting scheduled; confirm legal approvers.
- Week 1: Provide test dataset spec and residency requirements; Redwood to propose architecture variant (hosted EU / dedicated region).
- Week 2-3: Evaluation window (functional tests, latency checks, KV cache behavior) and security evidence (SOC 2 artifacts + audit hooks).
- Week 4: Legal review + procurement checklist; finalize pilot contract.
- Week 6: Pilot sign-off / go/no-go.

High-level evaluation deliverables: sample telemetry, token-cost projection per 1M requests, and a brief runbook for audit access. I flagged three unknowns in the workbook: country-level log retention variance, required encryption-at-rest key management, and any local on-prem requirements.

Rafael — I’ll send calendar options for Tues/Wed CET. Sophie / Marco — please drop Anna and Benoît as optional in the invite so they can join when available.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Appreciate the clear plan. Two quick notes from Platform side:
1) For the evaluation, can Redwood support an option that keeps logs (for debugging) in Ireland only? We need to validate that log export pipelines can be constrained to an EU region.
2) Do you have a recommended encryption-key management pattern for KMS integration? Our legal team usually prefers customer-managed keys.
